lines.text: It's called two-pot. But your retirement fund has three pots.
Pot one: the vested pot. Everything you saved up to 31 August 2024. The old rules still apply to it.
Pot two: the savings pot. One third of what goes into your fund from 1 September 2024.
Pot three: the retirement pot. The other two thirds, locked until you retire.
Your savings pot also got a once-off start: 10% of your vested pot, up to R30,000.
So if R1,500 a month goes into your fund, R500 goes to savings and R1,000 is locked away.
While you're still in the fund, only the savings pot can be withdrawn: once a tax year, from R2,000.
The full two-pot guide is on the channel. Follow for a new money rule every day.
So next time someone says two-pot, ask them: which of the three?
